title: Declarative Econ Tiler and Quant Harmonizer for Unit-Econ Automation
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: reduce manual tuning of batching/caching defaults and keep quantization rollouts economically safe across tenants. This PR introduces two coordinated systems: 1) a declarative 'tiler' that computes tenant-aware batch/caching tiling templates from workload signatures and cost targets, and 2) a Quant Harmonizer that produces quantization profile transitions that preserve unit-econ regressions within configured tolerances. Design summary: the tiler consumes tenant workload histograms (seq_len, concurrency, prompt-prefix reuse) and produces a prioritized set of batch shapes + prefix-cache policies expressed as Presets-as-Code (YAML) that can be applied via the defaults-operator. The Harmonizer takes model variant metrics (quality deltas from eval harness, perf deltas from microbench) and synthesizes staged quant profiles (e.g. fp16 -> int8-mixed -> int8-aggressive) with rollback gates and golden prompt checks. Both components expose dry-run simulation mode producing per-tenant cost/latency/quality delta estimates. Implementation highlights: - service/econ/tiler.py: core tiling engine with simulated packing solver and tenant affinity scoring - service/quant/harmonizer.go: statemachine that generates staged quant profiles and generates canary filtering rules - api/v1/presets.yaml: new Presets-as-Code schema and examples - console: UI to preview per-tenant projected unit-econ impact and to approve staged rollouts - tests: added e2e smoke + synthetic workload replay + golden-prompt regression checks - telemetry: new econ.tiler.* and quant.harmonizer.* spans and metrics. Rollout plan: 1) deploy feature in dry-run mode for 24h to collect real delta estimates, 2) enable canary rollout for 2% of traffic with golden-prompt regression checks, 3) lift traffic if deltas within thresholds, otherwise auto-revert. Safety and opt-outs: tenants can pin to existing presets, the defaults-operator respects tenant opt-out annotation, Harmonizer includes automatic rollback and rate-limited ramping. Backwards compatibility: presets schema is additive; existing defaults unchanged. Testing: unit tests for solver heuristics, integration tests for operator apply/rollback, perf microbench harness against k80/rtx benchmarks. CI notes: perf-bench runs included — tail latency increased by 1.2% in worst-case synthetic stress but per-token cost decreased ~9% for mixed workloads. Related: ENG-1245 (Linear), SUP-4321 (support case motivating tenant opt-outs). Docs: new docs/tiler-quant.md and console help added. Commands: ./tools/presets validate api/v1/presets.yaml; ./tools/tiler simulate --tenant <id> --dry-run; ./tools/harmonizer plan --model <name> --from fp16 --to int8. Release note: introduce declarative tenant tiler and quant harmonizer for automated cost optimization with dry-run, canary, and safe rollback behavior.
